name: autofeature
description: Build an entire feature end-to-end from a single prompt. Pipeline: interrogate → scope → product-review → plan → branch → implement (parallel specialists) → test → review → ship → test-manifest. Review lenses unified under /review [product|feature|market|scope]: /product-review (CEO/PM/flow-walker whole-product gaps & flows), /feature-review (focused opinion + build advice for one feature), /market-review (market demand, competitive gap & VC fundability with cited, re-verified research), /scope. Also /test (acceptance-test the live app — web/iOS/Android — by driving it like a user, building its own test plan from what was built), /fullrun (deploy verification) and /seo (SEO audit + fix). Ritchies platform: /ritchies (cross-repo API+web+iOS+Android feature builder, API-first + pick-clients) and /api-standards (behavior-preserving route→controller→service refactor), backed by a kotlin-compose-architect specialist. Award interpretation: /award-map maps an Australian modern award into rosterio-compliance-service enumeration-first — transcribe the clause list and sub-clause counts from the Commission's PDF, triage every clause against the closed rule vocabulary, then author SQL against a fixed work list that only shrinks, so gap discovery terminates instead of looping. A merged PR isn't live — Step 9.5 gates promotion to the one deployed database (no staging tier exists) behind a re-run of verify/award-verify/closure against it and explicit sign-off. /award-verify closes the gap closure can't: independent re-derivation of every rule row from its clause text alone, diffed against what shipped, with an adversarial pass only where readers disagree — coverage proves a clause was read, this checks it was read correctly. /award-drift is the manual, on-demand answer to whether the award's own wording moved since it was mapped — re-fetches the text, diffs clause-by-clause, flags when the pay database itself may need a fresh workbook, and re-authors with history preserved (closes the superseded row's operative_to rather than deleting it, since the engine already resolves shifts against operative_from/operative_to and a blind delete would silently break historical pricing). Model-tiered for cost — the fan-out runs on Sonnet/Haiku, Opus only for the few highest-judgment steps (tune in orchestrator/model-tiers.md).
